pick.headline: Reagan and Gorbachev meet in Geneva
pick.summary: On 19 November 1985 Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev met in Geneva for the first US-Soviet summit in six years.
pick.significance: The summit produced little on paper but began the personal relationship that led to the INF Treaty and the end of the Cold War.
pick.fbis: The East Europe report of 20 November 1985 carried bloc coverage of the first day of the Geneva summit, including Warsaw radio's review of the morning papers and notes on the agreed news blackout on the talks.

alternates.headline: NATO and Warsaw Pact sign the CFE Treaty in Paris
alternates.summary: On 19 November 1990 the members of NATO and the Warsaw Pact signed the Treaty on Conventional Armed Forces in Europe in Paris.
alternates.significance: The treaty imposed deep cuts in tanks, artillery and aircraft, ending the Soviet superiority in Europe that NATO planning had faced for forty years.
alternates.fbis: CTK reported on 18 November that President Havel had left for the Paris CSCE meeting, which was to ratify the treaty on conventional armed forces cuts.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: East Europe, No. 223, 19 November 1990
evidence.snippet: …18 (CTK)—Czechoslovak President Vaclav Havel left today for Paris, to attend a three-day meeting of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe (CSCE), beginning on Monday.
